ordered_diagnoses: Prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential
Small cell carcinoma of the prostate

key_facts: 1 week of difficulty voiding
Urinary retention requiring catheterization
Prostate-specific antigen level was 0.62 ng/mL
Normal complete blood count, routine chemistries, and tumor markers
Digital rectal examination revealed an enlarged prostate
Palpable nodules and ill-defined border on prostate
Pelvic ultrasound confirmed a heterogeneous prostatic mass
Magnetic resonance imaging showed a 5.5-cm heterogeneous lesion
Cystoscopy raised suspicion for bladder invasion
Positron emission tomography–CT and colonoscopy suggested rectal invasion

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large prostatic mass, difficulty voiding, and urinary retention, along with imaging findings of a heterogeneous prostatic mass and suspicion of bladder and rectal invasion, is more consistent with a sarcomatous process than adenocarcinoma, and the biopsy result supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential
rejected.why: While the biopsy result mentions this as a possibility, the aggressive nature of the patient's symptoms and imaging findings suggests a more malignant process

rejected.label: Prostate cancer
rejected.why: This is a broad term that encompasses many types of prostate cancer, but the specific findings in this case are more suggestive of a sarcomatous process

rejected.label: Prostatic adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's low PSA level and the presence of a large, heterogeneous mass are not typical of adenocarcinoma

rejected.label: Small cell carcinoma of the prostate
rejected.why: This type of cancer is typically associated with a higher PSA level and more systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case
